# What Docker access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone. Docker
# issues two kinds and writes a prefix for each: dckr_pat_ for a personal access
# token and dckr_oat_ for an organization access token.
#
# The two are read differently behind their prefixes, which the cases below are
# mostly about. A personal access token's body is twenty-seven base64url
# characters read as a count, so a token is thirty-six characters and the
# twenty-eighth character of a run belongs to no credential. An organization
# access token's is twenty-seven read as a floor, because the widths claimed for
# that kind disagree, so its body runs to the end of the run it stands in.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: the run and eleven more of it are a body of twenty-seven, and
# the run twice over is the thirty-two an organization access token is also
# written at. The cases that carry the alphabet's other letters are built from
# runs of their own instead, one per kind in each case: the digits and then the
# uppercase letters ascending, and the digits and then the lowercase letters
# ascending, each stopping at the count.

patterns: docker-access-token

# The prefix Docker writes a personal access token with, in the places a token
# is written: the environment a build reads it from, the command it logs in
# with, and the request that exchanges it for a bearer token.

case:     a personal access token in an environment assignment
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN=dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN=«docker-access-token»

case:     a personal access token in the command a user logs in with
in:       docker login -u myusername -p dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      docker login -u myusername -p «docker-access-token»

case:     a personal access token in the body a request exchanges it in
in:       {"identifier":"myusername","secret":"dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a"}
out:      {"identifier":"myusername","secret":"«docker-access-token»"}

case:     a personal access token in the file a workflow writes it into
in:       registry-password: dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      registry-password: «docker-access-token»

case:     a personal access token in a docker config.json
in:       {"auths":{"registry.example.com":{"auth":"dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a"}}}
out:      {"auths":{"registry.example.com":{"auth":"«docker-access-token»"}}}

case:     a personal access token between tabs
in:       field\tdckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a\tnext
out:      field\t«docker-access-token»\tnext

case:     a personal access token followed by crlf
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN=dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a\r\n
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN=«docker-access-token»\r\n

# The second prefix, in the places that kind is written: the response Docker's
# own specification prints one in when it is created, the request that exchanges
# it for a bearer token under an organization name, and the environment an
# automated build reads it from.

case:     an organization access token in the response it is created in
in:       {"token":"dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a"}
out:      {"token":"«docker-access-token»"}

case:     an organization access token in the body a request exchanges it in
in:       {"identifier":"myorg","secret":"dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a"}
out:      {"identifier":"myorg","secret":"«docker-access-token»"}

case:     an organization access token in an environment assignment
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN=dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN=«docker-access-token»

case:     an organization access token in the command a build logs in with
in:       docker login -u myorg -p dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      docker login -u myorg -p «docker-access-token»

# The alphabet the body is written in: base64url, which is the letters of both
# cases, the digits, the hyphen and the underscore. What it leaves out is the two
# characters standard base64 writes in place of the last of those, so a payload
# carrying either is no body. The prefixes are read in lowercase alone, since the
# uppercase spelling is the shape an environment variable's name is written in.

case:     a personal body carrying a hyphen and an underscore
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef-123456789_
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     an organization body carrying a hyphen and an underscore
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef-123456789_
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     a plus in the personal body
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef+123456789a
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef+123456789a

case:     a slash in the personal body
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef/123456789a
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef/123456789a

case:     a plus in the organization body
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef+123456789a
out:      dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef+123456789a

case:     a slash in the organization body
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef/123456789a
out:      dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef/123456789a

case:     a personal body of uppercase letters
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQ
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     an organization body of uppercase letters
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQ
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     a personal body carrying the lowercase letters past the run
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     an organization body carrying the lowercase letters past the run
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     an uppercase personal prefix
in:       DCKR_PAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DCKR_PAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an uppercase organization prefix
in:       DCKR_OAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DCKR_OAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     hyphens where the prefix carries its underscores
in:       dckr-pat-0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      dckr-pat-0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     the personal kind with one letter capitalized
in:       dckr_Pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      dckr_Pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     the organization kind with one letter capitalized
in:       dckr_Oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      dckr_Oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

# A kind of the right width that Docker writes no token with. The scan reads the
# kind between the opening and the separator rather than anything standing in for
# one, so a third word there opens no candidate.

case:     a kind Docker writes no token with
in:       dckr_xyz_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      dckr_xyz_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

# The lengths either side of twenty-seven, which is where the two readings part.
# No page of Docker's writes a length down for either kind, so both counts rest
# on the rules the published rulesets state. For a personal access token five of
# those rules agree and the count is used as a count: twenty-six characters are
# not a token, and twenty-eight are a token and one character that belongs to no
# credential. The second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the
# match — a boundary there would drop this token rather than trim it, and a real
# token written against a character of the alphabet would come through whole.

case:     a personal body of twenty-seven characters is a token
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     a personal body of twenty-six characters is not
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789

case:     an alphabet run longer than a personal token is a token and what follows it
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «docker-access-token»b

# For an organization access token one rule states thirty-two and nothing
# corroborates it, where Docker's own specification prints twenty-seven
# characters behind the prefix — an example that may be elided rather than a
# width — so the count is used as a floor and the floor is the lower of the two.
# Twenty-six characters are not a token, twenty-seven are, and so is the width
# the rule asks for; a run longer than the floor is a token to the end of that
# run, which is the price of reading it this way and is what the cases below are
# for.

case:     an organization body of twenty-seven characters is a token
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     an organization body of twenty-six characters is not
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789

case:     an organization body of the width the rulesets ask for
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     an alphabet run longer than the organization floor is a token to the end of it
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     a word joined to an organization token by a hyphen goes with it
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a-suffix
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     the same word behind a personal token stays in the text
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a-suffix
out:      «docker-access-token»-suffix

# What a token may be written against. A prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a personal access token after an underscore
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN_dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN_«docker-access-token»

case:     an organization access token after an underscore
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN_dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN_«docker-access-token»

case:     a personal access token after a letter
in:       xdckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      x«docker-access-token»

case:     a personal access token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a.
out:      the token is «docker-access-token».

case:     an organization access token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a.
out:      the token is «docker-access-token».

case:     a personal access token between multi-byte text with nothing between them
in:       日本語dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a日本語
out:      日本語«docker-access-token»日本語

case:     an organization access token between multi-byte text with nothing between them
in:       日本語dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a日本語
out:      日本語«docker-access-token»日本語

# Two tokens written together. Every character of both prefixes belongs to the
# alphabet a body is written in, so a token can begin anywhere inside the one
# before it: a prefix written twice with a body behind the second is a token from
# either prefix, the two spans overlap and the whole of it is redacted as one.
# Written without that overlap two personal tokens are separate values and both
# go, where two organization tokens are one run and so one redaction.

case:     two personal access tokens with nothing between them
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789adckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-access-token»«docker-access-token»

case:     two organization access tokens with nothing between them
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789adckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     a personal prefix written where a body would stand
in:       dckr_pat_dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     an organization prefix written where a personal body would stand
in:       dckr_pat_dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-access-token»

case:     one of each kind on one line separated by a space
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-access-token» «docker-access-token»

case:     two different personal tokens on one line separated by a space
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef-123456789_
out:      «docker-access-token» «docker-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. A prefix is nine characters of an
# alphabet of sixty-four, so a base64url payload long enough to spell one carries
# a candidate, and the twenty-seven behind it are in the alphabet by
# construction. That is the answer rather than a fault in it, because sparing it
# would spare a real token: the vendor's format is that prefix and that many of
# those characters, and no part of it is left for such a run to fail. Standard
# base64 and hexadecimal write no underscore at all, so neither carries a
# candidate at however long it runs.

case:     a personal prefix inside a longer base64url run
in:       payload=zzzzdckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789azzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«docker-access-token»zzzz

case:     an organization prefix inside a longer base64url run
in:       payload=zzzzdckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789azzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«docker-access-token»

case:     a standard base64 payload, which carries no underscore
in:       payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAdckrpat0123456789abcdef
out:      payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAdckrpat0123456789abcdef

case:     a hexadecimal digest, which carries no underscore either
in:       payload=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      payload=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

# And what this pattern leaves alone: a body a space has broken, under each kind,
# and two inputs carrying no prefix at all — a run of the right length opening
# with something else, and a line of prose, which holds nothing as long as a body
# and no run unbroken by a space.

case:     a personal body broken by a space
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef 123456789a
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef 123456789a

case:     an organization body broken by a space
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef 123456789a
out:      dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef 123456789a

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxx_xxx_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      xxxx_xxx_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And the shape Docker Hub's login endpoint took before a prefix was written in
# front of one, which the pattern's own file weighs: a UUID carrying nothing to
# be recognised by but the vendor's word beside it. Such a token reaching a log
# stays in the output whole, because a pattern reading it would redact every
# UUID a caller passes through.

case:     the shape a token took before a prefix was written in front of one
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a log line naming the registry a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="pushing an image" url=https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/library/nginx/tags
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="pushing an image" url=https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/library/nginx/tags
